title: Lists
cards/0/body: A ListBox shows a collection from the ViewModel. A DataTemplate describes how a single item looks.
cards/1/q: Inside a DataTemplate, where does {Binding Name} look for Name?
cards/1/options/0: On the current list item, the Person object
cards/1/explain: Each row's DataContext is its own item from the collection.
cards/2/title: Added it, but the list did not change
cards/2/body: A plain List<T> does not announce that an item was added. ObservableCollection<T> does, through the CollectionChanged event, and the ListBox shows the new row right away.
cards/3/q: People is a List<Person>. A command adds a person, but the list on screen does not change. Why?
cards/3/options/0: List<T> does not announce changes; you need ObservableCollection<T>
cards/3/explain: Same idea as PropertyChanged, but for collections.
cards/4/body: ListBox virtualizes by default: it creates controls only for visible rows and reuses them as you scroll. That is why a list of 100,000 items stays smooth.
cards/4/deep: Virtualization breaks if you put a ListBox inside a StackPanel: the panel gives its child infinite height, so the ListBox creates controls for every row. Give the list a bounded height, such as a star row in a Grid.
cards/5/explain: In Avalonia 11 it is ItemsSource. Items remains for items added directly in markup.
cards/6/q: Which line makes a 100,000-row list slow?
cards/6/explain: StackPanel gives the list infinite height, which turns virtualization off. Use a Grid with RowDefinitions="Auto,*".
cards/7/q: Match each term to its meaning
cards/8/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/8/options/0: A row's DataContext is an item from the collection
cards/8/options/1: ObservableCollection updates the ListBox on Add and Remove
cards/8/options/2: Changing a property inside Person also needs PropertyChanged on Person
cards/8/options/3: List<T> updates the ListBox on its own
cards/8/explain: ObservableCollection tracks which items are in it, not the properties of those items.
